routes.label: Condition on whether opposite neighbors have equal crops

question:
A farmer’s rectangular field is partitioned into a \(2\) by \(2\) grid of \(4\) rectangular sections as shown in the figure. In each section the farmer will plant one crop: corn, wheat, soybeans, or potatoes. The farmer does not want to grow corn and wheat in any two sections that share a border, and the farmer does not want to grow soybeans and potatoes in any two sections that share a border. Given these restrictions, in how many ways can the farmer choose crops to plant in each of the four sections of the field?

[Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_10A_Q18_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Number the four sections \(1,2,3,4\) clockwise. Each crop has exactly one incompatible crop, which cannot be placed next to it. Fix the crop in section \(1\), with \(4\) possible choices. Each of its neighbors, sections \(2\) and \(4\), then has the same three allowed choices.

If sections \(2\) and \(4\) have the same crop, there are \(3\) ways to choose it. They both forbid the same crop in section \(3\), leaving \(3\) choices there. This contributes \(3\cdot3=9\) arrangements.

If sections \(2\) and \(4\) have different crops, there are \(3\cdot2=6\) ordered choices. They forbid two different crops in section \(3\), leaving \(2\) choices. This contributes \(6\cdot2=12\) arrangements.

All four borders have now been checked. Multiplying by the initial choice gives \(4(9+12)=\boxed{84}\), choice C.
